original_question: Assume V is defined over a field F and has a fully idempotent root grading R that is a division grading, meaning that every nonzero x in a root space V_alpha makes Q(x)|V_alpha invertible on the opposite root space. In the low-rank cases 2 <= rank R <= 4, is it true that whenever the Steinberg group St(V, R) is not centrally closed, every root space V_alpha must be one-dimensional over F and the field F must satisfy exactly the exceptional small-field restrictions listed in table (3.2.1)?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the paper's low-rank open problem, namely Conjecture 1.1 in the introduction, read together with the adjacent Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3. The paper itself is an introduction with open problems, and the published chapter version occupies pp. 77–114. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01313))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content very closely: the base field hypothesis, the fully idempotent/division-graded setting, the low-rank range 2 <= rank <= 4, the conclusion about non-central-closedness of St(V,R), the forcing of one-dimensional root spaces, and the appeal to the exceptional small-field cases in Table (3.2.1). It also matches the paper's overall low-rank focus, which is exactly the part left open after the rank >= 5 central-closedness theorem discussed in the surrounding context. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/bfm%3A978-1-0716-0264-5/1))
missing_details: The ambient object should be stated as a Jordan pair V, not just a graded vector space V. The paper's Steinberg groups are attached to root graded Jordan pairs. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/bfm%3A978-1-0716-0264-5/1))

The rank condition should be tied to the underlying 3-graded root system (or irreducible/connected component, depending on the paper's exact introductory formulation), not left as an unqualified 'rank R'. The surrounding results distinguish connected or irreducible components carefully. ([page-one.springer.com](https://page-one.springer.com/pdf/preview/10.1007/978-1-0716-0264-5_6))

The phrase 'fully idempotent root grading' should be replaced by the paper's exact terminology and hidden data: idempotence is formulated via the existence of a suitable cog / full cog, not just informally. ([page-one.springer.com](https://page-one.springer.com/pdf/preview/10.1007/978-1-0716-0264-5_6))

The division hypothesis should be stated with the paper's exact quantifiers: for every root alpha and every nonzero x in V_alpha, the relevant Jordan-theoretic invertibility condition on the opposite root space is required. Your draft gestures at this correctly but does not make the quantification fully stand-alone. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))

The conclusion about the field should be phrased type-by-type: F should be one of the exceptional small fields appearing in Table (3.2.1) for the corresponding low-rank type, not 'satisfy exactly all restrictions' in a global sense. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))

It helps to make explicit that the statement is a conjectural necessary condition for failure of central closedness, not a theorem already established in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01313))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should identify St(V,R) as the Steinberg group attached to the root graded Jordan pair (V,R), since the paper studies several related groups such as PE(V) and universal central extensions. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/bfm%3A978-1-0716-0264-5/1))
refined_question: Let F be a field, let (R,R_1) be the underlying irreducible 3-graded root system of rank 2, 3, or 4, and let V be a Jordan pair with a fully idempotent division root grading (V_alpha)_{alpha in R_1} over F in the sense of the paper. If the associated Steinberg group St(V,R) is not centrally closed, must it follow that dim_F(V_alpha)=1 for every root alpha in R_1 and that F is one of the exceptional small fields listed in Table (3.2.1) for the corresponding type? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-63849-8_4))
justification: This refinement stays as close as possible to the paper's apparent official formulation: it keeps the exact low-rank obstruction theme from your draft, but restores the paper's natural ambient language of root graded Jordan pairs, ties rank to the underlying 3-graded root system, and removes the ambiguity in how Table (3.2.1) is to be read. It is also aligned with the broader structure of the paper/book: rank >= 5 is covered by the main central-closedness theorem, so the genuine unresolved issue is precisely the low-rank 2, 3, 4 range. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/bfm%3A978-1-0716-0264-5/1))
